record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: For ranked keyword search over a decentralized peer-to-peer document collection, how can the system collect and maintain the global statistics needed by state-of-the-art ranking functions, such as document-frequency information over the total collection, in a way that is simultaneously robust to failures, efficient in resource usage, and fully distributed?

evidence.quote: Collecting and maintaining these statistics in a robust, efficient, and distributed manner is a challenge.

artifact.category_tag: distributed ranking statistics in P2P search
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a peer-to-peer system consisting of a dynamic set of N autonomous nodes, where each node n stores a local collection D_n of text documents and peers may join, leave, or fail at any time. The union D = ⋃_n D_n forms a global document collection. A user issues a keyword query q = (t_1, …, t_k) at some node and expects a ranked list of the top documents from D under a ranking function R(d, q) that depends on global corpus statistics. Specifically, for each term t, let df(t) = |{d ∈ D : t ∈ d}| (the global document frequency) and |D| (the global collection size); typical ranking functions (e.g., TF–IDF or BM25 variants) require values such as idf(t) = log(|D|/df(t)) together with local term frequencies.

Design a fully distributed protocol that, in the presence of node churn and failures, allows every node to obtain, for any query term t, an estimate d̂f(t) of df(t) and an estimate |D̂| of |D| such that:
(a) (Robustness) The protocol continues to provide such estimates with bounded relative error ε with high probability even when an adversarially chosen fraction of nodes fail or depart between updates.
(b) (Efficiency) The expected per-node communication, storage, and computation costs grow sublinearly (ideally polylogarithmically) in N and in |D|.
(c) (Distribution) There is no central coordinator; every node executes the same protocol using only local state and messages exchanged with a bounded number of neighbours.

Provide such a protocol, together with a proof of its accuracy, robustness, and resource bounds, or establish impossibility results showing the optimal achievable trade-offs among (a), (b), and (c).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a high-level open challenge about maintaining global IDF-style statistics in decentralized P2P keyword search. Subsequent work (e.g., gossip-based aggregation, distributed sketches, Bloom-filter–based DF estimation, and various P2P IR systems such as MINERVA and Alvis) has proposed partial solutions, but no single protocol is established as a definitive answer satisfying all three desiderata simultaneously. The status is best described as unknown / partially addressed rather than formally solved.
